## Spatial discretization evidence {#sec-ch15-ch04-tests}

This catalogue accompanies @sec-ch04. The source pin is
`snapy@e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0`. It is a source inventory and a record of this
report's own CPU checks, not a run log: no compiled snapy test, no CUDA arm and no multi-rank
test was executed for this draft. The report's checks verify derivation identities and the
numerics of ported formulas in CPU float64 or in symbolic algebra; they cannot certify dispatch,
CUDA kernels, communication, or that the compiled code is the code that was ported.

### Independent report checks

Three scripts carry twenty-one claims, all passing, with their stdout committed beside them and
reproduced byte for byte. Each ports the formula from the file it cites rather than restating the
formula the chapter asserts.

`src/snapy_report/ch04/recon_check.py`, seven claims, ports the interpolants from `interp_cp2` to `interp_weno5`
([`interp_simple.hpp:43-153`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/recon/interp_simple.hpp#L43-L153))
and the selection in `create`
([`interpolation.cpp:6-39`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/recon/interpolation.cpp#L6-L39)):

| claim | what it establishes |
|---|---|
| `[C1]` | each centred face stencil reproduces cell averages of polynomials exactly to its nominal degree, found by raising the degree until it fails rather than by assertion |
| `[C2]` | the weno3 linear weights rebuild `cp3` exactly, symbolically, difference zero |
| `[C3]` | the weno5 linear weights rebuild `cp5` exactly, symbolically, difference zero |
| `[C4]` | measured face order in two regimes: design order with no critical point, and the fall of weno3 to 2.09 through two critical points while `cp3` keeps 2.99 |
| `[C5]` | the plm slope is the van Leer harmonic mean: TVD on random triples, zero slope at every extremum, centred in the smooth limit |
| `[C6]` | `interp_ppm` returns the cell value unchanged, so `type: ppm` is donor cell |
| `[C7]` | donor cell is first order at the face, fitted 1.00 |

`src/snapy_report/ch04/covariance_check.py`, six claims, ports `_flux_covariance`
([`hydro_forward.cpp:54-150`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp#L54-L150))
and the `x1_mass_covariance` block at
[`hydro_forward.cpp:314-344`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp#L314-L344):

| claim | what it establishes |
|---|---|
| `[C1]` | the mean of a product is the product of means plus $h^2/12\,f'g'$ to $O(h^4)$, by series expansion of both sides, with the remainder's leading coefficient printed |
| `[C2]` | the $x_1$ second moment of the face measure: exactly $h^2/12$ in Cartesian, $h^2/12 - h^4/(144r^2)$ on the curved $x_2$ or $x_3$ face |
| `[C3]` | the centroid offset vanishes identically in Cartesian and is $h^2/(12r) + O(h^4)$ on a curved grid |
| `[C4]` | the stored $m_1/\rho$ differs from the cell average of the velocity at fitted order 2.00, and the correction recovers it at 3.99 |
| `[C5]` | both corrections are bitwise zero at rest, not merely small |
| `[C6]` | the one-sided wall density slope is second order, fitted 1.98 |

`src/snapy_report/ch04/operator_check.py`, eight claims, ports `divergence`
([`coordinate.cpp:509-553`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/coord/coordinate.cpp#L509-L553)),
the spherical-polar `face_area1` and `cell_volume`
([`spherical_polar.cpp:178-211`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp#L178-L211))
and `lmars_impl`
([`lmars_impl.h:17-78`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/riemann/lmars_impl.h#L17-L78)):

| claim | what it establishes |
|---|---|
| `[C1]` | a uniform flux on a Cartesian block gives a bitwise zero tendency, not a round-off one |
| `[C2]` | the coded areas and volume give $\nabla\!\cdot\!(r\hat r) = 3$ to $3.6\times10^{-15}$ |
| `[C3]` | the cell volume is the exact radial integral; the midpoint form would be short by $h^3/12$ per unit solid angle |
| `[C4]` | the sum of $V$ times the divergence is the net boundary flux, on random face fluxes, so the operator is in flux form |
| `[C5]` | lmars is consistent: equal states give the exact physical flux to $8.9\times10^{-16}$ |
| `[C6]` | the face velocity carries the pressure jump over $\rho c$ and the face pressure the velocity jump times $\rho c$, each checked on its own |
| `[C7]` | the dry row plus every species row is the total mass flux, exactly, with three species |
| `[C8]` | the face-local index map is a permutation of the three momentum rows for each direction |

### Registered tests of the compiled code

These are registrations read from the source, not measured passes. `test_plm` asserts that a
constant field is reconstructed exactly for `dc`, `plm` and `weno5` in all three directions.
`test_weno` and `test_weno5_cuda_line` cover the WENO interpolants and the CUDA line.
`test_riemann` covers the registered solvers. `test_coordinate` covers the gnomonic areas and
volumes, the frame projections and the radial source. `test_cubed_sphere_cell_volume_python`
asserts the six panel volumes sum to the shell volume and the radial identity per cell at
$10^{-12}$. `test_radial_face_moments` asserts the curved face centroid shift and second moment
against exact rationals at $10^{-14}$. `test_hydrostatic` holds a six-panel isentropic shell at
rest over 100 steps below $10^{-8}$. `test_x1_seam_split_mp` matches a two-rank split against the
one-block answer at $10^{-13}$. The flux-covariance family is covered by
`test_flux_covariance_rows`, `test_flux_covariance_seams` and `test_horizontal_flux_covariance`.

### What is not verified here

The gaps matter more than the coverage, and they are listed rather than implied.

**No check of its own for HLLC.** @sec-ch04-hllc is the one scheme in the chapter with no ported
check. Its consistency, and that it resolves an isolated contact exactly, are properties of
textbook HLLC; neither is asserted by a test in the repository nor measured here. They should be
read as expected, not as verified. The same is true of the Roe solver, whose section is written
from reading alone, and of `plume-roe`, which no test selects at all.

**No render.** This machine has no Quarto and the book has no project file, so no chapter was
rendered for this draft and no cross-reference, figure cell or include chain is build-verified.
`tools/check_citations.py` does not exist either; the chapter's 191 citations were checked by a
local verifier for path, range and anchor at the pin, which is not the same as the gate passing.

**Ported, not executed.** Every claim above runs a numpy or sympy port of the formula, not the
compiled code. A divergence between the port and the compiled behaviour, from dispatch, from a
CUDA kernel or from a compiler, would not be caught. `[C6]` of `recon_check` is the one claim
whose subject is the absence of an implementation rather than its behaviour.

**Not measured anywhere.** The order of the corrected horizontal flux end to end has no committed
convergence ladder; the row and seam tests are the only evidence for it. The seam averaging is
shown to restore conservation and is not shown to be accurate: the size of the disagreement it
averages away is unmeasured. No test covers the reconstruction row split, so exchanging `interp1`
and `interp2` would be caught only by an accuracy test.

### Reproduction

Run `python3 src/snapy_report/ch04/recon_check.py`, `covariance_check.py` and
`operator_check.py`. Each exits with the number of failed claims and prints the lines recorded in
the sibling `.out`, which is committed and must match byte for byte. The two data figures of
@sec-ch04 read `src/snapy_report/ch04/data/*.json`, written by the same scripts, so a figure that
changes after a clean re-run is a defect.
